v1.feedback: The breathing-exhale mechanic is well-conceived and the warm amber flush during bloom genuinely delivers the 'gentle-explosion' surprise. The cool_a teal (0.18, 0.52, 0.42) sits at ~65% HSL saturation — push it toward a smokier sage (e.g. 0.25, 0.44, 0.38) to stay safely inside the earth-tone gate. Consider a very slow single-pass camera drift (e.g. 0.0002 on Z over 60s) so the vortex reveals depth over time rather than reading as a flat disc from the fixed vantage.

v2.feedback: Strong Aizawa form with a well-paced 28s breathing cycle — the bloom-as-gentle-explosion concept lands. The sage/bone/amber palette is exactly right. Two refinements: the radial push (1.8 * exp(-r*0.6)) is so gentle it barely reads as an 'explosion' even metaphorically — consider a brief moment where the outer shell visibly loosens before relaxing, perhaps with a faster exp decay so the core stays tight while the periphery blooms more. The amber flush during exhale is subtle to the point of near-invisibility; raising the mix factor from 0.7 to ~0.85 and widening the smoothstep window would let the color swerve register as an actual tonal shift rather than a whisper.
